title: Canadian astronaut part of historic Artemis II mission around the moon
desc: A new era of space travel is underway, and Canada is part of it. A major space mission is capturing attention around the world, and it includes a Canadian astronaut helping lead the way. Artemis II will send a crew of four astronauts around the Moon. It marks the first time humans will travel beyond low Earth orbit since the Apollo era more than 50 years ago. “It will be the first time since the Apollo program that astronauts travel beyond low Earth orbit,” said Abigail Sadowski, an astronomer with the Royal Astronomical Society of Canada. A proud moment for Canada Among the crew is Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen, who has also visited Moose Jaw, Sask., in 2024, making this a milestone moment for the country. “He is our very own Canadian,” Sadowski said. googletag.cmd.push(function() { if($(document).width()<900) { s = googletag.defineSlot('/50748803/dmj-all-bigbox', [300, 250], 'div-gpt-1648064270259-bbm1'); s.setTargeting('URL', [window.location.pathname]); s.setTargeting('position', [1648064270259]) s.setTargeting('story_id', 'canadian-astronaut-part-of-historic-artemis-ii-mission-around-the-moon'); s.addService(googletag.pubads()); googletag.pubads().refresh([s], {changeCorrelator: false}); } }); Hansen will become the first Canadian to travel around the Moon, putting Canada at the forefront of modern space exploration. A more inclusive space program The Artemis II crew reflects a broader and more inclusive future for space missions. The team includes the first woman, the first person of colour, and the first non-U.S. astronaut on a lunar mission. “That kind of representation matters,” said Sadowski. “It shows that space exploration is becoming something humanity does together, not just something done by a select few.” Related Stories: Artemis II mission carrying Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen targets April 1 launch Out of this world: Astronaut Jeremy Hansen visits Moose Jaw ▶️ Listen to this news story on the radio A step toward the future While Artemis II is a test mission, it plays a key role in preparing for future landings on the Moon and beyond. googletag.cmd.push(function() { if($(document).width()<900) { s = googletag.defineSlot('/50748803/dmj-all-bigbox', [300, 250], 'div-gpt-1648064270259-bbm2'); s.setTargeting('URL', [window.location.pathname]); s.setTargeting('position', [1648064270259]) s.setTargeting('story_id', 'canadian-astronaut-part-of-historic-artemis-ii-mission-around-the-moon'); s.addService(googletag.pubads()); googletag.pubads().refresh([s], {changeCorrelator: false}); } }); The mission will help test systems and operations needed for longer and more complex journeys. A message beyond space Sadowski says the mission is about more than science or technology. “I think Artemis II represents hope,” she said. “It shows that despite everything happening on Earth, we’re still capable of working together across countries and disciplines.” Inspiration close to home For students and aspiring scientists in Saskatchewan, the mission is also a reminder of what is possible. “Seeing a mission like Artemis II makes me feel like that dream is a little more real and a little more possible,” Sadowski said.
